newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end higher as yen tumbles.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end higher as yen tumbles.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended higher across the board on Tuesday, backed by the yen's steep fall against the dollar, traders said.
Trade was relatively buoyant in line with the volatile currency market, the traders said.
Gold prices ranged from eight yen to 15 yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark February ending up 14 yen at 1,399 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $348.85/349.25 per ounce at 0726 GMT, against $348.00/348.50 in New York on Monday.
The dollar hit a fresh 50-month high of 126.12 yen in Tokyo trade.

Gains in gold futures were partly offset by profit-taking from private investors, while trade houses sold spot gold in arbitrage dealing earlier in the day. "Despite selling pressure from Japan earlier in the day, spot gold prices were relatively firmer, supported by short-covering from overseas producers," a trading house trader said.
Traders said, however, private investors held massive longs in yen-based gold and platinum futures, and further gains are likely to be capped by long-liquidation.

In platinum and palladium market, buying interest from overseas investors was strong during Asian hours, backed by the fresh delay in Russian exports of the metals to Japan, but private investors were wary of building fresh longs at the current levels. Platinum futures ranged from five yen to 25 yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark February ending up 19 yen at 1,460 yen.
Benchmark February palladium was up 14 yen per gram at 579 yen. Benchmark February silver was up 3.9 yen per 10 grams at 196.1 yen.
